summary: Heinrich Rückert was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1845–1852) and the University of Breslau (~1852–1875).
Heinrich Schliemann worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in approximately 1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe. He taught at the University of Zurich (Privatdozent 1841, associate professor 1849, Ordinarius 1864) and local schools.

Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (~1863–1867), studying under Hermann Brockhaus. He subsequently served as a classical languages teacher at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD), and Leipzig, learning under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, and held a habilitation post at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under Rudolf von Roth, Siegfried Goldschmidt, Wilhelm Scherer, Albrecht Weber, and Ernst Windisch. His posts included Berlin, Greifswald (1881), Heidelberg, and Columbia University.

Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS, and Heidelberg, and held posts at Heidelberg University (1965) and the University of Tübingen, where he was chairholder from 1973 to 1998.

Heinz Adolf Mode worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University, Basel, and under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, later serving as professor of Oriental archaeology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Erich Frauwallner and Ernst Waldschmidt, holding posts at Saarland University, Mainz, and as Chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1965–2000).

Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Vanderbilt and Chicago under Joseph Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith, holding posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith University (1990–1992), and Harvard University from 1992, including directing the Reischauer Institute.

Helen J. Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Paul B. Watt and held a post at the University of Hawaiʻi, attested in 2006.

Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and has served as Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum since around 1991.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, as attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979 to 1984. She held a post at Rice University beginning around 1990.

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1960–1967) and served as a research associate at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.
Hellfried Dahlmann worked in linguistics and related fields. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg from ~1936 to 1951 and at the University of Cologne from ~1951 to 1971.

Hellmut Wilhelm was a sinologist who studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught German at Peking University (~1933–1948) and held the chair of sinology at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

Hellmuth Hecker was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (1942–1948, PhD) and under Paul Debes in 1945, later serving as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from ~1952 to 1988.

Helmer Smith worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner, later holding posts at Lund University (1921) and as professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Humboldt University, Hamburg, and Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm, subsequently holding a post at the University of Bonn from ~1974 to 2001.
